openTomorrow: Yes, absolutely. I need this accountability every single day. Tomorrow morning I'm logging my workout first thing—it's part of my routine now to stay focused and keep my mind off cravings.
secured: I think it means my data is private and encrypted. That's why I chose this app over telling people in my life. I don't need judgment, just quiet tracking.
freeze: Maybe it's a way to pause the challenge temporarily if life gets too hard? I hope I don't need it, but it's good to know it's there if I slip up.
selfReported: It means I'm being honest about my distance and time. The app trusts me to input real numbers and eventually take a photo as proof. It's about building integrity with myself.
best: Setting up the challenge and actually committing. For 45 years I've made excuses. Today I didn't make one. I logged in and I'm doing this.
worst: The empty input fields staring at me, knowing tomorrow I have to actually fill them with real numbers. No hiding. No lying to myself.
tellFriend: No. Not yet anyway. This is between me and myself. If I tell someone, it becomes their business and their disappointment. I need to prove to *myself* I can do this first. Maybe after 30 days.
